call_points.text: FY27 revenue growth guided at 75% over FY26, with consolidated EBITDA margin of 20-22%.
Business is H2-heavy: 70-75% of annual revenue is expected in H2, as in prior years.
Received a 200 MW LOA from NLC India in July, a repeat order.
Receivables are expected to fall significantly over the next 3-4 quarters as equipment supply replaces turnkey EPC.
Management sees only force majeure, such as the Middle East crisis, as a risk to meeting guidance.
Analysts pressed on repeated guidance misses; management said the equipment pivot will show results mainly from Q3.
INOX Green received NCLT Ahmedabad approval for the Wind World India acquisition; formalities expected in Q2FY27.
Demerger of INOX Green's power evacuation business into INOX Renewable Solutions completed with record date August 1, 2026.
Consolidated revenue guided to grow by around 75% over FY26.
Pivoting towards 75-80% equipment supply to ease working capital cycle.

timeline.summary: Inox Wind filed its Q4FY26 Monitoring Agency Report showing ₹1,249.25 Cr of ₹1,249.33 Cr Rights Issue proceeds utilised with zero deviation.
Inox Wind Q4FY26 revenue at ₹1,151 Cr; PAT at ₹91 Cr
Inox Wind reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,306 Cr and issued strong FY27 growth guidance.
Inox Wind Limited shared the audio recording of its Analyst/Investor Conference Call held on May 29, 2026, at 17:00 hrs (IST) via its website.
Inox Wind hosted its Q4 FY26 earnings conference call on May 29, 2026, highlighting a 3.1 GW order book and a strategic shift towards equipment supply.
On 7 August 2026, Inox Wind's Q1FY27 earnings call maintained FY27 guidance of 75% revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin, with Q1 revenue at ₹872 Cr and an order book of ~4.4 GW.

watchlist.response: Management attributed misses to the turnkey-to-equipment pivot and said results will show mainly from Q3; it did not give quarterly numbers.
watchlist.text: Repeated guidance misses over the last three quarters despite management confidence.

watchlist.response: Receivables are accounted under Ind AS 115 on risk transfer and some are stuck until commissioning; they are expected to fall significantly over the next 3-4 quarters as equipment supply rises.
watchlist.text: Trade receivables are significantly higher than peers.

watchlist.response: Management maintained the annual guidance, citing H2 weighting and flexibility in equipment supply, but declined to quantify quarterly growth.
watchlist.text: Whether the 75% growth guidance is achievable given flat Q1 revenue.
